name: Victims Family
label: Alternative Tentacles
lede: Two Santa Rosa teenagers, a one-year Canadian ban, a Dutch radio hit, and a stretch when Green Day and Mr. Bungle were the openers.

eras.title: Two Santa Rosa teenagers and a tape
eras.text: Ralph Spight and Larry Boothroyd start a trio in Sonoma County, book a summer tour off cassette demos, and get a look from Jello Biafra. The debut LP lands on Mordam.

years.src: Wikipedia: Victims Family · Music Life Radio · CBS San Francisco: 40th anniversary · Grokipedia
years.h: Two teenagers in Santa Rosa start a band named after a cartoon
years.p: [[Ralph Spight|3ed0757e-311e-4acb-8f31-d7107e944ed1]] (guitar, vocals) and [[Larry Boothroyd|1526e291-6dcd-4f25-8b3c-01bef9fad8c1]] (bass) form Victims Family with drummer Devon VrMeer.
years.xp:
Wikipedia and CBS San Francisco both say Spight and Boothroyd were teenagers when they started. The name comes from a cartoon by B. Kliban, according to the 2014 Music Life Radio profile of Spight. Wikipedia says the first show was at the Kennilworth Recreation Center in Petaluma.

Grokipedia dates the founding to October 1984; the other sources say only 1984.

years.cap: Larry Boothroyd, bass guitarist for Victim's Family, onstage in San Francisco. · Wikimedia
years.h: A cassette demo gets them a national tour and Jello Biafra's ear
years.p: Booked off tapes alone, the trio plays Albuquerque with [[NOFX|dcaa4f81-bfb7-44eb-8594-4e74f004b6e4]], then opens for the [[Dead Kennedys|37c78aeb-d196-42b5-b991-6afb4fc9bc2e]] and the [[Descendents|f035837e-4117-438d-a524-cacf43500e68]] at the Novato Theater.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the 1985 U.S. tour was arranged from cassette demos, and that the Dead Kennedys and Descendents bill is where [[Jello Biafra|2280ca0e-6968-4349-8c36-cb0cbd6ee95f]] noticed them. Tales of Terror and Social Unrest are also named on shows from the run.

Wikipedia adds that early gigs included opening for Faith No More and Suicidal Tendencies.

years.src: AllMusic: Victims Family · CBS San Francisco: 40th anniversary · Victims Family: Biography
years.p: The debut. CBS San Francisco notes it took on topics like homophobia, when few punk records did.
years.xp: The AllMusic bio has them signing to Mordam Records in the mid-1980s, and Mordam put out their first three albums. The Victims Family site describes it as an angry brew of off-kilter rhythms and cut-and-paste histrionics.

years.src: Wikipedia: Victims Family · Victims Family: Biography
years.h: An Oakland pizza parlor gig starts a friendship with Nomeansno
years.p: Playing a pizza place with the Canadian trio [[Nomeansno|37e9d7b2-7779-41b2-b2eb-3685351caad3]] leads to years of shared bills and, in 1990, a producer.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the Oakland pizza parlor show to 1986 and calls it the start of a lasting friendship. Nomeansno's [[John Wright|5530ccc3-9bdc-4472-a356-31d621fc6378]] later produced White Bread Blues and The Germ. In 2009 and 2010 the two bands were still sharing stages, including a run in the Czech Republic.

eras.title: Banned from Canada, opening for Nirvana
eras.text: A border ban, three drummers, a European tour and a Dutch radio hit. By the end, Mr. Bungle and Green Day are opening for them.

years.h: Canada bans them for a year after a U.S. tour
years.p: Wikipedia says the ban followed their 1987 U.S. tour, which also put them on bills with Capitol Punishment and Scratch Acid.
years.xp: Wikipedia gives no reason for the ban.

years.src: Wikipedia: Victims Family · AllMusic: Victims Family · CBS San Francisco: Elbo Room
yt: Live: Things I Hate To Admit, Tribal Area
years.h: Things I Hate to Admit LP, recorded at Prairie Sun in Cotati
years.p: Second album, Mordam again. It is also where a friendship with [[Primus|84dc4f23-c0b8-4fe1-bbca-a3993ddc8fc2]] begins, with the two bands sharing stages repeatedly.
years.xp: Wikipedia has the album recorded at Prairie Sun Studio in Cotati, in 1988, and dates the Primus friendship to the same year. AllMusic lists the record as 1989; Wikipedia and CBS San Francisco say 1988.

years.src: Wikipedia: Victims Family · Grokipedia: Victims Family
years.h: Amsterdam invites them over; Eric Strand replaces Devon VrMeer
years.p: Konkurrent Records asks the band to tour Europe, and Strand takes the drum stool for the trip.
years.xp: Wikipedia has Strand replacing the departing VrMeer for the European tour, invited by Amsterdam's Konkurrent Records. Grokipedia says Strand's stint ended over creative differences mid-tour and that longtime roadie [[Tim Solyan|add5effa-1139-4e4b-a880-09d9a90bda00]] took over.

years.src: Wikipedia: Victims Family · Grokipedia: Victims Family
years.h: Roadie Tim Solyan takes over on drums
years.p: Solyan is the drummer on the records that follow, from White Bread Blues on.

years.big: One of the outstanding punk albums of the decade
years.src: CBS San Francisco: 40th anniversary · Wikipedia: Victims Family · AllMusic: Victims Family · Victims Family: Biography
years.h: White Bread Blues LP, produced by Nomeansno's John Wright
years.p: That is CBS San Francisco's verdict, and John Wright of Nomeansno produced it. The single "Caged Bird" reaches number 16 on Dutch VPRO radio's chart, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Wright, drummer of [[Nomeansno|37e9d7b2-7779-41b2-b2eb-3685351caad3]], produced the record on Mordam. AllMusic dates the album 1991; the band's own bio and Wikipedia say 1990. The Victims Family site says it lifted them to headlining slots across Europe and North America.

years.src: Wikipedia: Victims Family · CBS San Francisco: Elbo Room
years.h: On the road with Tad and Nirvana
years.p: Wikipedia says the trio supported [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] and [[Tad|867d3fb7-9cd1-47a4-a8f0-de29cdca2004]] in 1990, a run that cemented them as a live act. Mr. Bungle and Green Day, then unknown, were opening for them at home.
years.xp: CBS San Francisco repeats the Nirvana and Primus bills as the calling card, and Wikipedia says [[Mr. Bungle|277e21a9-2d64-452d-96c4-2d23a7af5891]] and [[Green Day|084308bd-1654-436f-ba03-df6697104e19]] often opened. The exact dates of the tour are not given in these sources.

eras.title: Alternative Tentacles, a break, a return
eras.text: A move to Biafra's label, a burnout break, then a reunion show at the Kennel Club and two more records before the first ending.

years.cap: Cover art "Yellow Head" by Harvey Stafford
years.src: Wikipedia: The Germ (album) · Wikipedia: Victims Family
years.h: The Germ: first record on Jello Biafra's Alternative Tentacles
years.p: Seventeen tracks in 38 minutes, produced again by John Wright. Wikipedia says the band left Mordam for the move.
years.xp:
The Germ is credited to Alternative Tentacles and Konkurrent. AllMusic gave it 2.5 stars and called it a break from traditional hardcore, hearing Screaming Trees and Meat Puppets in places. Track titles include "I Pissed on a Tree."

Touring took its toll, and the band took a break after the record, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Victims Family · Alternative Tentacles: Victims Family
years.h: A sold-out Kennel Club show ends the break
years.p: Back in San Francisco after a break, the band fills the Kennel Club.
years.xp: Alternative Tentacles' bio also says road fatigue led to the breakup and a 1993 reformation.

years.p: The band's fifth album, released a year after the Kennel Club return.
years.xp: Scaruffi dates it 1993; Wikipedia and the band's bio say 1994.

years.src: Wikipedia: Victims Family · AllMusic: Victims Family
years.h: Four Great Thrash Songs, recorded live at the Melkweg, Amsterdam
years.p: Recorded at the band's last show at Amsterdam's Melkweg, per Wikipedia; the band winds down after it.
years.xp: AllMusic says the band disbanded around 1995. Wikipedia's infobox lists Tim Solyan's first stint as 1989 to 1994.

eras.title: Hellworms and one more record
eras.text: Spight and Boothroyd keep playing in other bands, then cut Apocalicious with a new drummer.

years.src: Wikipedia: Victims Family · AllMusic: Victims Family
years.p: After Hellworms fold, Spight and Boothroyd bring in Gleza for a reunion album on Alternative Tentacles, then tour it, including two SXSW trips and European dates.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the touring wore out Gleza and the band went on indefinite hiatus after. Side projects during the years apart include Saturn's Flea Collar and Hellworms, per Wikipedia and the band's bio.

eras.title: Reunions, a split LP and forty years
eras.text: A twentieth-anniversary weekend turns into a habit: European tours, a 2012 single, then a split LP in the fortieth year.

years.src: Bottom of the Hill: 2004 · Wikipedia: Victims Family
years.h: Twentieth anniversary: the Phoenix Theatre, then Bottom of the Hill
years.p: Two nights, Petaluma and San Francisco, celebrating every incarnation of the band. Tim Solyan is on drums for both.
years.xp: Bottom of the Hill's own calendar confirms the December 12 night. Wikipedia says the shows celebrated all incarnations. Wikipedia's infobox lists Solyan as drummer from 2004 to the present.

years.h: Alternative Tentacles turns 30; then Czech dates with Nomeansno
years.p: Victims Family play the label's 30th anniversary shows in 2009 with Alice Donut, then tour the Czech Republic with [[Nomeansno|37e9d7b2-7779-41b2-b2eb-3685351caad3]] in 2010.

years.src: Wikipedia: Victims Family · CBS San Francisco: Elbo Room
years.h: "Have a Nice Day" single and a thirteen-show European return
years.p: Wikipedia says the tour included the band's first Finland shows.
years.xp: The 7-inch on Alternative Tentacles was their last new music until 2024, according to CBS San Francisco.

years.src: CBS San Francisco: 40th anniversary · Wikipedia: Victims Family
years.h: In the Modern Meatspace, a split 12-inch with Nasalrod
years.p: Their first new music since 2012, on Nadine Records, shared with a Portland band they met in January 2019.
years.xp: The split came out earlier in 2024. The band marked forty years with a sold-out show at the Big Easy in Petaluma on November 30, per CBS San Francisco. Wikipedia adds three Pinback shows that month and three Canadian dates with Dead Bob in December.
